claims: The new GitHub checks break setup for non-GitHub origins. `scripts/bootstrap/codex-cloud-setup.sh:177-223`, called at `:556-557`: the two new checks have no such skip; `gh repo view` fails when no remote points at GitHub, so setup now exits under `set -e` with a bare `gh` error
the write probe would push to whatever origin is set, GitHub or not (`codex-cloud-setup.sh:177-223`)

The probe branch will start a Vercel deployment on every fresh setup. `codex-cloud-setup.sh:206`, `ui-dashboard/vercel.json:6-10`: `codex-cloud-write-probe-*` isn't on that list; every setup leaves a cancelled deployment record, or a full preview build runs with the production-scoped preview secrets in scope

Probe branch names can collide. `codex-cloud-setup.sh:192`: the name is `$(date +%s)-$$`, so two containers starting in the same second would pick the same name and one setup fails with "created the temporary write probe but could not delete it"
The Playwright install is fatal. `codex-cloud-setup.sh:537`: here a failure aborts the whole setup, while the sister script `claude-code-web-setup.sh:141-152` deliberately makes this step non-fatal
The Playwright install prints no guidance. `codex-cloud-setup.sh:537`: unlike every other fail-closed step, it doesn't print a hint naming `CODEX_CLOUD_INSTALL_PLAYWRIGHT_DEPS=false`

The outbound-hosts list leaves out the apt mirrors. `docs/notes/codex-cloud-setup.md:59-70`: `--with-deps` needs the distro mirrors, e.g. `archive.ubuntu.com`, and the `gh` apt fallback needs them too, so allowlisting exactly the listed hosts makes the Playwright step fail

"Verify shipping capabilities" doesn't check pull-request write access. `codex-cloud-setup.sh:184-185`; docs `:46-47`: a token with pull-request read-only passes setup, then `gh pr create` fails mid-ship
If the repo is public, both API reads succeed with any valid token, so they prove very little (`codex-cloud-setup.sh:184-185`)
a failed `gh api` call gives a raw error with no permission hint, unlike the other checks

the maintenance script never refreshes Chromium. `scripts/bootstrap/codex-cloud-maintenance.sh:99`: on a branch that bumps `@playwright/test`, a cached container keeps the old browser and browser tests fail with "Executable doesn't exist"
Stale text: `claude-code-web-setup.sh:9-13` still says that script is the one that "additionally installs Playwright Chromium"
Stale text: `codex-cloud-setup.sh:133-134` still asks for "repo/read PR permissions"
Stale text: `scripts/gate/routing-table/arms-scripts.mjs:261` still labels the test as "Foundry installer contract changed"

judge_reasoning.3846756487: Finding 6 says setup only makes a pull-request read call, though the docs require PR read/write. A token with PR read-only would pass setup, then gh pr create fails.
judge_reasoning.3846756810: Finding 1 says verify_origin_git_auth skips non-GitHub origins (CODEX_CLOUD_ORIGIN_URL), but the two new checks lack that guard and call gh / push to origin unconditionally.
judge_reasoning.3846756918: Not matched. The review's 'Checked and cleared' section says 'a failed delete doesn't retry' and treats that as correct. It never flags that created=false stops the EXIT trap fallback from retrying cleanup.
judge_reasoning.3846756922: Finding 3 says the $(date +%s)-$$ probe branch name can collide across containers with the same PID in the same second, and suggests adding randomness.
judge_reasoning.3846757143: Finding 2 names a concrete side effect of the probe really creating a branch on origin on every setup run (a Vercel deployment). That is the same underlying problem of mutating the remote, even though the suggested fix is an ignore rule rather than --dry-run.
judge_reasoning.3846757191: Finding 5 says the outbound-hosts list omits the apt/distro mirrors that playwright install --with-deps needs, so the Playwright step fails under a strict allowlist.

1.why: verify_github_api_capabilities (setup.sh:177-186) calls `gh repo view` with no non-GitHub skip, unlike verify_origin_git_auth:158-161. This is the same issue as known item :179.

2.why: verify_origin_write_access pushes to origin with no GitHub-host guard. Known items :179 (missing non-GitHub skip) and :231 (probe mutates the real origin) already cover this.

3.why: ui-dashboard/vercel.json only disables `sentry-autofix/*`, so the probe push does start a Vercel deployment. This is a side effect of the probe mutating origin on every run, which known item :231 covers.

4.why: The probe name is `$(date +%s)-$$` at :192, which is the same as the known item 'Make the temporary branch name globally unique'.

5.why: The Playwright step is fatal, but that is on purpose: the docs say setup fails closed on tool installation and give CODEX_CLOUD_INSTALL_PLAYWRIGHT_DEPS=false as the opt-out. It is a design preference, not a defect.

6.why: Many other fail-closed steps also print no env-var hint (pnpm install, several Foundry error paths), so 'unlike every other' is inaccurate. The opt-out is documented in the runbook. This is UX polish.

7.why: The docs host list (md:59-70) leaves out distro apt mirrors. This is the same as known item md:70 'Document the distribution package source'.

8.why: Only GET repos/{r} and GET .../pulls are probed (:184-185), which is the same as known item :195 'Verify pull-request write access'.

9.why: The point that the read-only API probes don't prove the needed permissions is the same weakness known item :195 raises about probing only read access.

10.why: verify_github_api_capabilities has no failure handling or heredoc hint. Under set -e a failing `gh api` aborts with a raw gh error, while the sibling origin-auth and write-probe checks print permission guidance.

11.why: codex-cloud-maintenance.sh only runs pnpm install, codegen and context-check, and never runs `playwright install`. Chromium installed by the new setup step goes stale when a branch bumps Playwright.

12.why: claude-code-web-setup.sh:9-13 still says 'this one additionally installs Playwright Chromium', but this change makes codex-cloud-setup install it too.

13.why: setup.sh:133-134 still says 'repo/read PR permissions', but the updated docs now require Contents read/write and pull-request read/write.

14.why: arms-scripts.mjs:261 reason is 'Codex Cloud Foundry installer contract changed'. At base the suite was Foundry-only, but it now also covers Playwright and the write probe, so the label is stale.
